title: Versatility
paragraphs: “Me? You mean as a comrade?”
“…That’s right.”

Let’s just leave it at that. Since there’s a chance that Itsuki might start a religion, I need to take precautions to prevent him from brainwashing his allies. As long as he doesn’t hold strange ideals about his comrades, he won’t go down that path.

To begin with, the difference in death counts between Ren and Itsuki is just one. But it’s probably better to let them think there’s a bigger gap. After all, they’ve both lost to me and Father multiple times.
“Ugh… That’s kind of scary. But still, on this journey… When fighting alone instead of as heroes, having allies will be important. It’s tough to keep fighting by yourself.”
“Ren likes being alone, so it might not be a problem for him.”
“That may be true! But I want to follow Naofumi’s advice. He said that by adapting to others, we can eventually reach greater heights.”
“Naofumi-san also mentioned that having allies who follow you is important, right?”
“For now, I guess Motoyasu’s Filolials will be helping us out…”
“Eclair-san is protecting Naofumi-san, after all.”
“Indeed. I’m gathering Filolials, so we’ll never be short on allies!”
Not just 100 like last time—200, 300, or even 1,000 if a miracle happens! Just as I was thinking that, Ren and Itsuki gave me half-lidded stares.
“I mean, they’re useful, but isn’t it kind of weird for almost all your allies to be Filolials?”
“Do you have a problem with that?”
“…You’re seriously saying this, aren’t you?”
“Still, eventually, we should gather more allies.”
“Yeah.”
What’s so great about humans? What could they possibly dislike about the angelic beings that are Filolials?
“By the way, where are Yuki and the others?”
“They got bored and went to help Naofumi with level grinding.”
“Ah, that’s right. It does feel strangely quiet without them around.”
Now that it’s been pointed out, aside from our conversation, there’s hardly any noise. The only other sound is the distant hustle and bustle of the town.
“You’re the main source of noise, Motoyasu.”
Ren and Itsuki watched me as I worked. Fufun! This is Yuki-chan’s outfit! I proudly showed it off.
“Naofumi’s specialty is cooking, and Motoyasu’s is sewing… Maybe I should learn a craft too.”
“You mean something outside of weapon skills, right?”
“Yeah.”
“By the way, Father mastered alchemy, crafting, and potion-making in the first world. He also taught us Melromarc’s writing system.”
“Just what the hell is that guy…?”
Ren sounded exasperated. What’s so strange about it? Well, future Father had already spent several months in another world by then, so it’s only natural.
“That’s too many skills…”
“What about us?”
“Ren learned blacksmithing. I don’t know how skilled he became, though.”
If I recall, he was taught by the blacksmith in the village. He spent his time hunting, training, or practicing smithing with Éclair, I believe?
“It does seem like an interesting field. Did I make anything good?”
“I wouldn’t know. I only heard that you crafted various things in the village.”
“Did I use self-made weapons?”
“The blacksmith you trained under and the weapons shop owner in Melromarc were so skilled that your work left little impression.”
“Does learning it even matter? Though I guess… having some skills is better than nothing.”
“Um… What about me?”
“I have no idea.”
As for Itsuki, I truly have no clue. All I remember is that he was always with Stalker Pig.
“Even looking back at all the previous loops and the first world, I don’t recall you ever doing anything in particular.”
“So I was completely Naofumi-san’s freeloader?”
“Wait a minute, Motoyasu. What were you doing?”
“I was running a Filolial ranch.”
“And sewing?”
“Only for the Filolials.”
For some reason, Itsuki looked visibly relieved. Don’t lump me together with some mere freeloader—I was running a respectable Filolial ranch!
“Motoyasu was basically a freeloader too, Itsuki, so don’t worry.”
“Ren-san, just because you supposedly learned blacksmithing doesn’t mean you get to look down on me.”
“Hmph, well, if you pick up some skills outside of combat, you might have a better chance against Naofumi.”
“Ugh…”
“That said, blacksmithing requires equipment, so it’s not something you can just learn on the fly.”
“Then maybe I should learn how to do laundry or cleaning. That would be useful for our travels.”
“Itsuki, that’s filthy!”
“Ren-san, you should just focus on blacksmithing. Someday, you can make us top-tier equipment.”
“Until then, I refuse to be treated like a freeloader!”
Ren and Itsuki had started arguing. What a lively bunch. Should I stop them?
“Fighting is bad, I say.”
“This isn’t a fight! We’re discussing the rules for communal living!”
“But can you even compete with Father when it comes to housework?”
“Considering Naofumi-san’s skill in cooking, it’s hard to believe he wouldn’t also be good at cleaning. That guy is a full-fledged househusband.”
“More importantly, why is he so skilled? And mostly in domestic areas! Didn’t he live with his family? Usually, the parents handle that stuff.”
“I heard he was an otaku. Maybe his family treated him poorly?”
“Ah… Maybe he was the lowest in the family hierarchy, so he learned those skills just to live how he wanted.”
Ren clicked his tongue. Why the tongue click? What’s that supposed to mean?
“Guess I have no choice… I’ll learn how to butcher animals.”
Ren muttered this, and Itsuki visibly flinched.
“Ugh… I never thought there’d come a day when I’d actually envy Ren-san for being summoned as the Sword Hero…”
“All I can do with a bow is hunting, and that’s not much different from before.”
“Itsuki, don’t you have any other skills, like something cultural?”
“I took various lessons when I was younger…”
“Judging by your appearance, you seem like the type to dabble in refined activities—music, for example.”
“I did learn piano and violin in elementary school. But they weren’t that interesting to me.”

Oh! So Itsuki can play instruments. I’ve messed around with an electric guitar before. Well, not enough to call it a hobby. I only learned a little because some pigs I knew were into it. I even attended a concert once.
“I knew it.”
“Ren-san, you probably have experience in kendo, right?”
“There were training programs in VR. Since there’s no physical exhaustion online, most people in my world learned some kind of combat skill.”
What kind of warrior race is that?
“Wow… That sounds convenient. Did you do anything else?”
“Cooking simulations through apps, but I wouldn’t stand a chance against Naofumi. That guy’s a freak.”
“I can cook too! Though I’m no match for Father. I lived alone for a long time, after all.”
“The range of household skills here is ridiculous. Naofumi-san is way too overpowered!”
“Wait, we don’t have to let Naofumi do everything. If we focus on cleaning and laundry, we might have a shot at keeping up.”
“Let’s do our best to stop the Naofumi monopoly. And while we’re at it, we can pick up some useful skills too.”
“Maybe we could even take over some of his alchemy duties.”

As they talked, I finished making Yuki-chan’s outfit. Eventually, Ren and Itsuki, exhausted from their debate, started questioning why they were even learning skills that might become unnecessary once we reached Faubrey. But at the same time, they admitted it might still be worth it. And so, as the sun began to set…
“We’re back!”
The others had returned.
“Naofumi, I won’t lose to you!”
“Huh? What are you talking about?”
“Yes, one day, we’ll be as multi-skilled as you!”
“Again, what are you talking about!?”
“Things are pretty lively over here. But it was just as noisy on our end.”
“Vroom!”
“Sakura-chan and the others were running around full of energy.”
“Yeah! Sakura is super energetic!”
Father patted Sakura-chan on the head.
“Ah—me too, pat me!”
“Alright, alright. Kou, you were a good boy too.”
“Motoyasu-sama! I did my best!”
“I know, Yuki-chan. You worked really hard.”
“So, Motoyasu-kun, did you finish the clothes?”
“Of course, they’re all done!”
As usual, I showed off the outfits I had made for Yuki-chan and the others.
“Whoa… That’s a completely gothic-style dress.”
“Motoyasu-san really has a distinct sense of fashion.”
“Sakura-chan, Kou, since Motoyasu-kun made these just for you, why don’t you try them on?”
Father led Sakura-chan and the others into another room. Except for Kou—he stayed here.
“Okay!”
Kou started changing into his outfit here. Well, since his outfit was for a boy, I designed it to be easy to move around in.
“Iwatani, how do I put this on?”
“The first person you ask is Naofumi?”
“He’s basically the mom of the group.”
“Ren, Itsuki, shut up.”
Father scolded them for analyzing him like that.
“If the outfits for Sakura-chan and the others are too complicated, we can ask Motoyasu-kun, but Eclair was with them, so it should be fine.”
“Yeah, if Éclair’s there, she should be able to help them dress.”
“She seems kind of clumsy, though. Are we sure it’ll be okay?”
“Well, nobles don’t usually dress themselves, right? And Éclair does seem pretty noble-like…”
Right then, Éclair returned with Yuki-chan and the others, now dressed.
“Oh, everything went fine?”
“What do you mean?”
“I heard some nobles don’t even dress themselves.”
“Maybe in Faubrey, but I’m from Melromarc. Father was a strong supporter of demi-humans.”
“I don’t really know much about that, but…”
“Ah, right, you’re from another world. But now you know—I can dress people just fine.”
Éclair glanced at Father. Oh, I see how it is.
“Housework, huh?”
“I only ever studied the sword.”
“What about academics? Like, reading, writing, or general education?”
“That’s basic stuff. It would be strange not to know it.”
“And yet, you can’t cook…”
“Enough about me! Look at them!”
So, we all turned our attention to Yuki-chan and the others. I did too. They still looked as adorable as angels.
“Wow… It really suits them. Probably because they were already cute to begin with.”
“They look like child idols from TV.”
“No, aren’t they even cuter? I’ve never seen kids this perfect-looking before.”
“Yeah. Even I, who don’t know much about this kind of stuff, can tell they could become celebrities in no time. Their beauty rivals that of the cutest avatar models in games.”
“Yeah… I always thought characters like this only existed in novels, anime, or manga.”
“Well, we are in another world. Maybe this whole thing is like a manga or anime.”

Everyone was showering Yuki-chan and the others with praise. Yuki-chan puffed out her chest as if it were only natural. On the other hand, Sakura-chan and Kou just tilted their heads as they leaned against Father like usual.
“Naofumi, food!”
“Kou too!”
“Alright, alright. You two care more about dinner than your looks, huh?”
“What a waste of potential.”
“Well, it’s fine, isn’t it?”
“Shall we get going? I think we’ve stayed here long enough.”
“Yeah. I feel something… off outside the inn. Maybe people are starting to figure out who we are.”
“Agreed. Let’s move out.”
And so, we hurriedly set off. Our destination—Faubrey.
“Sakura-chan, everyone, just hold on a little longer. Once we’ve traveled a bit, we’ll have dinner.”
“Okay!”
“We’ve already paid for the inn, so we’ll use magic to temporarily conceal ourselves before taking the carriage.”
“Yeah, we’re all set.”
“Right. We may be a bit tired, but we can’t afford to stop now.”
“I’ve got remedies for motion sickness prepared, so let’s get moving.”
“I’m looking forward to the journey.”
“Alright, let’s go!”

And so, we quickly left the inn and set out. We almost got stopped by what seemed to be messengers from Siltvelt. If they had realized we were Heroes, they would have had justification to act. With that near-miss behind us, we headed toward Faubrey.
